current_answer: DigitalOcean Startups now shows an application path for an AI-native startup without a VC, incubator, or accelerator: select “Other” in its application. New applicants must have raised USD 10 million or less, use a company website and matching email, and create a business-email DigitalOcean team account. The issuer says credits last 12 months but that the amount varies; it does not publish a fixed direct-applicant award, country map, or review time. Standard credits exclude several GPU products and third-party AI models hosted outside DigitalOcean infrastructure, so this is an application route—not a budget you can safely build around.

catalogue_card.question: Can a startup apply without a VC—and know its DigitalOcean credit?
catalogue_card.text: You can submit without a VC, incubator, or accelerator. DigitalOcean does not publish the direct-applicant award, so confirm the balance and service coverage before you build around it.

summary: DigitalOcean lets a founder without a VC, incubator, or accelerator submit an application by selecting “Other.”
It prioritises AI-native startups and lists USD 10 million or less raised, a company website and matching email, and a business-email team account as new-applicant checks.
DigitalOcean says credits last 12 months and that the amount varies; it does not publish a fixed direct-applicant award, country map, or review time.
Standard credits exclude several GPU products and third-party AI models hosted outside DigitalOcean infrastructure.
A direct application is a route to check, not a runway number to budget.
uncertainty: DigitalOcean does not publish a fixed direct-applicant award, country-availability map, review time, or applicant-specific GPU-credit outcome.
DigitalOcean’s standard credits exclude several GPU products and third-party AI models hosted outside DigitalOcean infrastructure; confirm the awarded service coverage before choosing a workload.
UKRI’s detailed organisation and individual eligibility rules decide whether a particular applicant can lead the sustainable-AI project.
AWS does not publish country coverage, credit validity, or selection criteria above USD 1,000 on reviewed pages.
Azure for Startups coverage and verification rules remain unconfirmed.
Individual-grant coverage is still narrow and not a worldwide inventory.
